lines: לוּ נֵלֵךְ בְּדֶרֶךְ תָּמִיד בְּצֵל כְּנָפָיו

review: The hymn is the marriage of the Lamb: 1:1–3 is Isa 62:11 (הִנֵּה יִשְׁעֵךְ בָּא) with Rev 22:12, 2:1–3 Rev 21:4 (וְלֹא־יִהְיֶה־שָּׁם עוֹד מָוֶת … וְלֹא נְהִי), 3:1–3 1 Pet 2:9–12, 4:1–3 Heb 11:13 (גֵּרִים וְתוֹשָׁבִים) with John 14:2, and 5:1–3 Rev 19:7–9.

The refrain is identical in stanzas 1–4 and switches to the second person in stanza 5 (וּבִכְבוֹדְךָ), because the printed Arabic itself changes from وَبِمَجْدِهِ to وَبِمَجْدِكَ in the last stanza: by then the Bride is addressing the Bridegroom, not speaking of Him.

1:2 הָרִיעוּ — the Arabic وَاهْتِفُوا is a shout, and the Hebrew keeps the distinction between רִנָּה (singing) in line 1 and תְּרוּעָה (the shout) here and in 5:3; both are cultic words (Ps 47:6, הָרִיעוּ לֵאלֹהִים בְּקוֹל רִנָּה).

2:2 יַעֲבֹר וָיָסַף — the Arabic تَغِيب is simply 'vanishes'; the Hebrew uses the doubled verb of Job 14:10's passing-away idiom so the cloud has the weight of a thing that is really gone. The line is one verb longer than the Arabic, which the printed metre absorbs.

5:2 לַחֲטִיפָה — the Arabic الاِخْتِطَاف is the rapture; חֲטִיפָה is post-biblical for a snatching-away, and the line needs it rather than a paraphrase, because the whole stanza hangs on the Bride waiting for that one event. Glossary entry added.
